# The failing scenario for the import-direction boundary, as a fixture rather
# than as prose. `just lint-boundary` feeds this file to ruff twice: once as if
# it lived inside the vendored ESPHome directory, where every import below is
# banned, and once as if it lived beside the adapters, where all of them are
# ordinary. The first run has to fail and the second has to pass.
#
# The bare `import reachy_mini_ha_satellite` below is the one TID251 cannot
# express — banning the package root would ban the vendored modules' own relative
# imports, which ruff resolves to absolute paths before matching. The recipe's
# second half greps for it instead, and requires this line to be here so that half
# is proved to fire too. Do not remove it.
#
# It is a .txt so that nothing else picks it up — it is not linted by `ruff check
# .`, not type-checked, and not collected as a test. Its only readers are the
# recipe, through `ruff check --stdin-filename` and grep, and
# `scripts/vendored_provenance.py`, which knows it is original to this repository.

import reachy_contracts
import reachy_mini
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.adapters
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.assets
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.behaviour
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.config
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.main
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.ports
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.wake_word
import reachy_mini_ha_satellite.web

# Dynamic forms, which TID251 cannot see at all — it inspects import statements.
# The grep half catches these, qualified or not, and this is what proves it.
import importlib

importlib.import_module("reachy_mini")
__import__("reachy_mini_ha_satellite.adapters")
